contexts.text: He has caught impressions that...
The things which are impressed on the memory from sensuous things.
According to the impressions from (the objects of the senses)...
Thus there is impressed on him the image of Heaven.
For (falsities and evils) when once impressed on any scientific, remain.
A paper... which appeared as if printed with types.
The truth so impressed becomes persuasive truth.
(After death) from the idea impressed, they remain like themselves.
When the truths of faith have been thus impressed... they... become familiar...
As this idea has been impressed on them, it is permanent...
Impression on the life then. Signified.
To write = to impress on the life.

Truths Divine impressed on the life by the Lord. Signified. Truths are said to be impressed on the life when they become of the will and thence of the act. So long as they stick merely in the memory, and so long as they are only regarded intellectually, they are not impressed on the life...
The reason to write = to impress on the life, is that writing is for the sake of recollection to all posterity: the same is the case with the things impressed on a man's life. Explained.
On which are impressed the truths and goods of the Spiritual Kingdom... Signified.
To engrave on stones = to impress on the memory.
See whether it is allowable to insert these things when the time comes for printing.
The impression made on Spirits... by singing and music.
That in the other life impressions about others are eradicated with very great difficulty.
Impressions such as it was insinuated into me to say, are either insanities... which are easily expelled; but the impressions in which anyone has confirmed himself... remain so...
Therefore those words ought to be in constant use, on which an idea has been once impressed.
He who is in charity and in true conscience... has each and all things (of the Decalogue) as it were impressed on him, so that he has no need to learn them.
The Angels especially inflow into his truths of faith and into his goods of charity, which have been impressed on him... SE 4620.
In the world they had... spoken about others, and had given an impression...
See Imitate.
